investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never reached the VM provisioning step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler reports "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" for those 2 nodes and "node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" for the other 4, leaving 0/6 nodes available. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion or misconfiguration condition, not an eval infrastructure or code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of a broader service outage or user-traffic impact is present in the supplied packet.

Because the eval pod could never be scheduled, the remote agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state check produced zero evidence — all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the Kata/PeerPods VM resource pool on the production-api Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving remote agent pods in production-api has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. With 0/6 nodes available — 2 due to Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch — every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod fails immediately as Unschedulable. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two kata-capable nodes. As a result, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returns a live agent, the state-polling step is never reached, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) receives no evidence at all.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never reached the VM provisioning step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler reports "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" for those 2 nodes and "node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" for the other 4, leaving 0/6 nodes available. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found"). This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion or misconfiguration condition, not an eval infrastructure or code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of a broader service outage or user-traffic impact is present in the supplied packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message indicating that the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource are fully exhausted and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never received a response and all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) confirms that every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of broader user-traffic or incident signals is present in the packet.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are at capacity, making the effective schedulable pool size 2 rather than 6.

Tertiary — preemption disabled or ineffective: the scheduler message 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod' and 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling' on the 2 eligible nodes indicates no lower-priority pods exist to evict, suggesting the capacity is held by equal- or higher-priority workloads or that preemption is not configured for this resource type.
